To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the asymptotic behaviour of the Vlasov Poisson-Fokker-Planck system is studied in the whole space and in bounded domains.

we have proved the large time asymptotic behaviour for the solutions of the VlasovPoisson-Fokker-Planck system in bounded domains with the reflection-type boundary conditions and the behaviour of solutions for the physical constants using the diffusion approximation method.
We prove the asymptotic behaviour of the Vlasov- Poisson-Fokker-Planck equation in the frictionless (p = 6 = 0) case in the whole space R6 and in bounded domains.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following problems.
the study of the asymptotic behavior of the VPFP system in the whole space and in bounded domains.

the study of the VPFP system in the frictionless and friction cases, in the whole lRs, in bounded domains, with respect to the constants of the system and in the asymptotic behaviour for the solutions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the asymptotic behaviour of solutions to the VPFP system is well understood in the frictionless situation, but not in the frictional one.
the VPFP system has a very rich mathematical structure.

(i) the large-time behaviour of the solutions of VPFP is given by a stationary solution of the Vlasov equation; (ii) the large-time behavior of the solutions of Vlasov-Poison-Fokker-Planck system with respect to the friction constant p is given by the Vlasov Poisson system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

in the case p = 0 and 6 = -1, the solutions to VPFP converge to a solution of the Vlasov equation, while in the case p # 0 or 6 # -1 the solution to the VPFP system is asymptotic to a solution of a Vlasov-Poissonequation.
the solutions to VPFP system in the large time behave asymptotically like the solutions to the Vlasov equation.
the VPFP system can be considered as an intermediate model between the VP system and the Foker-Planck equation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have been able to prove the asymptotic behavior for the VPFP system in the whole space.
we have been able to prove that the solutions of the VPF equation converge to the solutions of the Fokker-Planck equation.
we can use a diffusion approximation method to study the large time asymptotic of the Vlasov Poisson Fokker Planck system.
